key_insight: HEAR is a bidirectional protocol that lets the agent harness share workflow intent and lets the inference engine return runtime state, enabling more efficient agentic LLM serving without changing model or workflow semantics.
engineering_relevance: It gives systems builders a reusable control plane for cache-aware scheduling and execution-mode selection under memory pressure and concurrent agent workloads.
method: Standardizes harness→engine messages for workflow dependencies, context lifecycle, and execution requirements.
Returns engine→harness signals such as queue state, KV-cache status, resource pressure, and capabilities.
Separates protocol semantics from optimization policy so different coordination strategies can plug in without redesigning the stack.
evidence_signal: Across four benchmarks under memory-constrained concurrent serving, HEAR delivered up to 1.61× batch speedup and 2.23× lower median time-to-first-token on SCBench, with additional end-to-end speedups of 1.23× on BrowseComp-Plus and 2.45× on DeepResearchBench.
watch_item: Adoption depends on integrating the protocol into both harness and engine stacks, and the gains may vary with workload mix, cache pressure, and the chosen coordination policy.
paper_title: Can Agent Harnesses and Inference Engines Hear Each Other? The HEAR Protocol for Agentic LLM Serving
